evidence.rationale: Disabling stale accounts removes valid authentication paths available to adversaries.
Disabling stale accounts removes valid authentication paths available to adversaries.
Dormant domain accounts can retain broad access; disabling them removes stale domain credentials from the attack surface.
Disabling inactive local accounts reduces stale local credential abuse, dependent on endpoint/server coverage.
Disabling inactive cloud/SaaS accounts removes abandoned identities usable for access, persistence, or privilege abuse.
Disabling dormant accounts removes stale accounts that may still have breached or reused credentials, reducing credential-stuffing success against abandoned identities.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
